faqs.q: Sec. 62-62. - Interference with staff, faculty, or students of educational institutions.
faqs.a:
(a)
Short title.
This section is known and may be cited as the "School Interference Ordinance."
(b)
Legislative declaration; purpose.
The city council recognizes that education is crucial to developing the intellectual
               capacity of citizens and preparing them to become independent and productive members
               of society. It has also determined that disruptive or criminal behaviors at educational
               institutions interfere with proper learning environments and negatively impact educational
               progress. The city council further finds that measures that protect students, staff,
               and others in educational institutions are necessary to protect the health, safety,
               and welfare of the public. The purpose of this section is to place on notice those
               who are on or upon the premises or facilities of any educational institution that
               they may not impede the lawful performance of the duties by school staff or faculty,
               and that they may not disrupt, impair, interfere with, or obstruct the processes,
               procedures, or function of the educational institution.
(c)
Definitions
. As used in this section unless the context requires otherwise:
Chief administrative officer
means a person designated as the principal, vice-principal, or dean of an educational
               institution, or a person occupying a position similar to that of a principal, vice-principal,
               or a dean, and includes any designee of the principal, vice-principal, or dean charged
               with maintaining order on the school premises and in its facilities.
Credible threat
means a threat or physical action that would cause a reasonable person to be in fear
               of bodily injury.
Fight
means to engage in or take part in any type of loud or disruptive verbal disagreement
               or argument, or to engage in or take part in any physical scuffle or struggle, including
               but not limited to biting, boxing, elbowing, grabbing, hitting, kicking, pinching,
               pulling, punching, pushing, scratching, shoving, slapping, spitting, or throwing an
               object at another person, except as part of a previously scheduled and school-sanctioned
               amateur contest of athletic skill.
Impede
means to delay, hamper, hinder, obstruct, or otherwise interfere with the discharge
               of any school official's duties, or the ability of any student to pursue his or her
               educational activities, even momentarily.
Order
means a command, direction, or instruction by a school official to do, to discontinue,
               or to refrain from doing something. This includes, but is not limited to verbal direction
               to "get back," "let go," "stop," "stop fighting," "step away," or "step back," or
               other language or action by a school official that a reasonable person would view
               as direction to do, to discontinue, or to refrain from doing something.
School official
means any person employed by any educational institution, or any person duly authorized
               by the chief administrative officer of an educational institution to act as a volunteer
               in or in a volunteer capacity for that educational institution.
(d)
Unlawful acts.
(1)
Deny use or movement.
It shall be unlawful for any person located on or near the premises or facilities
               of any educational institution, to willfully or recklessly deny to students, school
               officials, or invitees:
(i)
Lawful freedom of movement on the premises;
(ii)
Lawful use of the property or facilities of the institution; or
(iii)
The right of lawful ingress and egress to the institution's physical facilities.
(2)
Impede performance.
(i)
By use of restraint or intimidation.
It shall be unlawful for any person located on the premises of any educational institution
               or at or in any building or other facility being used by any educational institution,
               to willfully or recklessly impede a school official of that institution in the lawful
               performance of his duties, or to willfully or recklessly impede a student of the institution
               in the lawful pursuit of his educational activities through the use of restraint,
               abduction, coercion, or intimidation or when force and violence are present or threatened.
(ii)
By engaging in a fight.
It shall be unlawful for any person located on the premises of any educational institution
               or at or in any building or other facility being used by any educational institution,
               to willfully or recklessly impede a school official of that institution in the lawful
               performance of his duties, or to willfully or recklessly impede a student of the institution
               in the lawful pursuit of his educational activities by engaging in a fight or by engaging
               in activities that reasonably appear to the school official to be a fight requiring
               the intervention of the school official.
(iii)
By refusing to discontinue a fight.
It shall be unlawful for any person located on the premises of any educational institution
               or at or in any building or other facility being used by any educational institution,
               to willfully or recklessly impede a school official of that institution in the lawful
               performance of his duties by refusing to obey an order of the school official to discontinue
               or stop fighting.
(3)
Refusal to leave premises.
It shall be unlawful for any person to willfully or recklessly refuse or fail to
               leave the property of or any building or other facility used by any educational institution
               upon being requested to do so by the chief administrative officer, if such person
               has committed, is committing, threatens to commit, or has incited or is inciting others
               to commit any act which would disrupt, impair, interfere with, or obstruct the lawful
               missions, processes, procedures, or functions of the institution.
(4)
Threat.
It shall be unlawful for any person to knowingly make or convey to another person
               either in person, in writing, or by electronic means a credible threat to cause bodily
               injury against a person the actor knows or believes to be a student or school official
               of an educational institution, or against a person the actor knows or believes to
               be an invitee who is on the premises of an educational institution.
(e)
Affirmative defense.
It shall be an affirmative defense to subsections (d)(1), (d)(2)(i), or (d)(3) that
               the defendant was exercising his right to lawful assembly and peaceful and orderly
               petition for the redress of grievances, including any labor dispute between an educational
               institution and its employees, any contractor or subcontractor, or any employee thereof.
(f)
Penalty.
Any violation of this section shall be punished by a fine or imprisonment not to
               exceed the limits established in
section 1-5
of this Code.
(Ord. No.
4767
, § 1, 7-19-2021)
